Description

Receptor tyrosine kinases connect to RAS through adaptors, shown here for the EGF receptor. EGF binds the extracellular domain of EGFR, and two EGF-bound receptors dimerise through a direct contact between the receptors [1]. In the dimer the receptors phosphorylate each other on tyrosines of their C-terminal tails. The adaptor GRB2 binds directly to phosphotyrosine 1068, less to tyrosine 1086, and indirectly through SHC [2, 3]. GRB2 binds the receptor through its SH2 domain [4]. Through its two SH3 domains GRB2 binds the proline-rich C-terminal tail of SOS1, the exchange factor of RAS [5-8]. The GRB2:SOS1 complex binds the activated receptor and so brings SOS1 from the cytoplasm to the plasma membrane, where RAS is [5, 9]. Bringing SOS1 to the membrane is enough to activate the RAS pathway [10].
